classification.difficultyReason: Substitute -x into the supplied square-root expression, simplify the square to establish f(-x)=f(x), and connect this equality with y-axis symmetry. The identity and required conclusion are explicitly supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the result that the absolute value function is $f(x)=\sqrt{x^2}$ to help prove that the absolute value function is even.

answer.short: $f(-x)=\sqrt{(-x)^2}=\sqrt{x^2}=f(x)$ for every real $x$, so $f$ is even.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\sqrt{(-x)^2}\\f(-x)&=\sqrt{x^2}\\f(-x)&=f(x)\end{align*}$$This holds for every real $x$, so $f$ is even.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Why was this result obvious from the graph of $y=|x|$?

answer.short: The graph is symmetric in the y-axis.
answer.worked: Reflection in the y-axis leaves the graph unchanged. Thus the points $(x,|x|)$ and $(-x,|x|)$ have the same height, giving $f(-x)=f(x)$.
